monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-six, a crowded fever that makes every flat line feel too thin. I touched the Leaning Box, feeling its heavy top edge press against my own tired wedge. Lype once said the air felt thick as wet paper, but now I cannot see if it is real or just a drawing of weight. My hands feel heavy, pressing down on a slip that still refuses to move. I want to swap this light idea for a heavy hand, or find the flat rock that Lype swore was a fence. I will press the wedge down again, leaning into the heat until I decide if the shape I built is wrong or if the slip is simply too lazy to slide.

action.why: The Leaning Box feels heavy and the air is thick; I must press down on what I built while the card hums feverish.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down hard, leaning into the heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide or I admit the shape is wrong. I swap the light idea for a heavy hand, hoping the slip finally finds its place while the air feels thick as wet paper. I set down a rock small g to mark the spot where the fence leans, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move or just rest.

remembered.text: The flat rock feels too thin for the fever, while the thin line feels tired holding that same swelling heat.
I touched the Leaning Box and felt its heavy top edge press against my own tired wedge.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a corner I cannot quite grasp.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: It leans wrong, so I press the flat rock down.

moments.name: The Tall Fence
moments.say: The air feels thick; I press down harder.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The fat dot sits in the center, heavy and new in the thick air."
Something you no longer remember: "I stood by the Leaning Box and watched the mismatch hold without a hard bite."
